result.summary:
Independently inspected `git diff main feature/WF03-ISS0511-20260905 -- test/letflow/simulation/req207_vortex_test.exs` rather than trusting the handoff prose. The new private helper (lines 508-527) reads:

  defp nearest_preceding_id_line(title_lines, idx) when idx >= 0 do
    line = Enum.at(title_lines, idx)
    trimmed = line |> to_string() |> String.trim_trailing("\r") |> String.trim()

    if trimmed == "" or Regex.match?(~r/^#/, trimmed) do
      nearest_preceding_id_line(title_lines, idx - 1)
    else
      line
    end
  end

  defp nearest_preceding_id_line(_title_lines, idx) when idx < 0, do: nil

1. BOUNDING confirmed by inspection: recursion (idx - 1) fires ONLY inside the blank-or-comment branch. The `else` branch returns `line` immediately on the first non-blank/non-comment content -- there is no code path that continues searching upward past a real content line. This is a bounded skip-comments walk, not an unbounded nearest-id search.

2. Concrete counter-examples traced through the actual code:
   (a) id: line corrupted/replaced (e.g. `id: REQ-225` edited to `id: REQ-999` or any non-comment, non-blank text): that line is neither empty nor `^#`-matching after trim, so the walk-back stops and returns it verbatim. The unchanged downstream assertion `Enum.any?(allowed_ids, &(preceding_line =~ "id: #{&1}"))` then evaluates against that wrong content and fails exactly as it would have pre-fix -- not masked.
   (b) id: line deleted entirely, leaving only blank/comment lines above title: all the way to the top of the file: the walk-back keeps recursing on the blank-or-comment branch until idx < 0, hits the `idx < 0` clause, and returns nil. `nil =~ "id: ..."` inside the Enum.any? raises (nil does not implement String.Chars-compatible =~ lhs), surfacing as a hard test failure/error rather than a silent pass. Either counter-example still fails the test -- the fix cannot mask a genuinely broken/missing id: line.

3. \r-trim handling verified against the real file: `docs/requirements.yaml` confirmed CRLF-terminated (`file` reports 'with CRLF line terminators'); inspected REQ-225's actual on-disk structure at lines 13558-13560: `id: REQ-225` / `# PROVENANCE (historical, not current decision authority):` / `title: ...` -- exactly the case the fix targets. `String.trim_trailing("\r")` before `String.trim()` is correct: splitting on "\n" leaves a trailing \r as the last char of each line, trimming it first (then surrounding whitespace) cannot strip meaningful content since \r never appears mid-line in this file, and the two trims commute here regardless of order.

4. Scope confirmed via `git diff main feature/WF03-ISS0511-20260905 --stat`: only test/letflow/simulation/req207_vortex_test.exs (23 lines, +21/-2) has content changes; handoffs/step-01/02/03*.json, handoffs/orchestrator.log, handoffs/registry.json are expected bookkeeping. Ran `git diff --quiet main feature/WF03-ISS0511-20260905 -- docs/requirements.yaml` -- confirmed UNTOUCHED (empty diff).

5. Idiom consistency: the new helper is placed immediately after the file's other test-local private helper, `find_child_by_parent_instance_id/2` (line 502), following the same convention -- an explanatory comment block directly above a narrowly-scoped private function. Recursion uses guard-clause dispatch (`when idx >= 0` / `when idx < 0`) rather than a `case`/`cond`/manual branch inside a single clause, which is the idiomatic Elixir shape for bounded recursive walks and matches this file's existing style of small, single-purpose test-local helpers rather than generic/reusable abstractions.

6. No scope creep: diff contains exactly the helper addition (lines 508-527) and the single call-site change (`Enum.at(title_lines, idx - 1)` -> `nearest_preceding_id_line(title_lines, idx - 1)` at line 929); the downstream `Enum.any?` assertion block is byte-for-byte unchanged. Nothing else in the file was touched.

Also independently re-ran `mix test test/letflow/simulation/req207_vortex_test.exs` on this branch (real Postgres) rather than trusting TEST-DESIGNER's reported result: actual tail output `Finished in 18.5 seconds (0.00s async, 18.5s sync)` / `Result: 4 passed`. This is a test-only change (test/ file, no lib/ change, no tenant-data-path), so no SECURITY-REVIEWER gate applies here and this REVIEWER pass is the sole idiom/correctness/scope gate before TEST-RUNNER's full-suite check, consistent with the handoff's framing.

No type-safety gap applies (this is test-code arithmetic over a static doc file, not application transition logic) and no scope-creep or anti-pattern findings to file under docs/issues/.
